lss.summary: The workstation exhibits significant ergonomic strain and motion waste. With 22% of time spent on NVA activities, primarily walking and bending, the operator is at high risk for musculoskeletal issues. Improving the workstation layout and material presentation will reduce both waste and safety violations.

lss_cards.title: Reduce bending and awkward postures with height adjustment
lss_cards.observation: Frequent bending (15s at 32-47s) and awkward postures observed throughout the cycle.

evidence.note: Deep bending while working on the vehicle frame.

lss_cards.root_cause: Work surface is too low, forcing the operator to bend deeply to reach components.
lss_cards.recommendation: Install a height-adjustable lift table or tilting stand to bring the work to an ergonomic height.

lss_cards.title: Optimize layout to eliminate walking waste
lss_cards.observation: Operator walks repeatedly during the cycle, totaling 8 seconds of motion waste.
lss_cards.root_cause: Parts and tools are located outside the immediate reach zone, requiring unnecessary movement.
lss_cards.recommendation: Rearrange the workstation into a compact cell and bring parts closer to the point of use.

safety_actions.action: Implement ergonomic height-adjustable fixtures to eliminate deep bending during assembly.
Adjust tool suspension heights to ensure all work remains below shoulder level.
Review tool orientation and handle design to reduce wrist strain.

operator_questions.question: I saw a 4-second walk at 00:13. Are you moving to fetch a part, or is the tool located away from the assembly area?
You are bending for 15 seconds starting at 00:32. Is the current height of the frame causing discomfort?
